verse_renderings.text: So then, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm in the Lord in this way. I love you and long to see you. You are my joy and my crown, dear friends.
I appeal to Euodia, and I appeal to Syntyche: share the same mindset in the Lord.

Yes, and I ask you too, my loyal partner, to help these women. They struggled alongside me in the work of the good news, together with Clement and the rest of my coworkers, whose names are in the book of life.

reader_notes.text: The Greek pictures a victory wreath. Paul means that the believers themselves are his honor and reward.
Paul repeats the same appeal with each woman’s name, placing equal responsibility on both. “Mindset” continues a recurring theme in this letter.
The Greek literally says “genuine yokefellow.” The person’s identity is unknown, and the expression may possibly be a personal name.
The Greek uses the same “struggle together” word used for the whole church’s shared effort in Philippians 1:27.
This is a biblical image of God’s secure record of those who belong to Him and receive eternal life.
